nodes.name: Nonexistence of the free particle in finite-dimensional quantum mechanics
nodes.statement: Assume $\hat{p}$ and $\hat{H}$ are non-zero finite-dimensional Hermitian operators. If $\commut{ \hat{H}, \hat{p} } = 0$ then there is no finite-dimensional linear operator $\hat{x}$ such that $i \commut{ \hat{H}, \hat{x} } = \hat{p}$.
nodes.section: 3 Revealing Inconsistencies in Finite-dimensional Quantum and Classical Mechanics
assumptions: Assume $\hat{p}$ and $\hat{H}$ are non-zero finite-dimensional Hermitian operators.
conclusions: then there is no finite-dimensional linear operator $\hat{x}$ such that $i \commut{ \hat{H}, \hat{x} } = \hat{p}$.
nodes.statement_short: No finite-dimensional $\hat{x}$ can satisfy $i\commut{\hat{H},\hat{x}}=\hat{p}$ when $\hat{p},\hat{H}$ are nonzero, Hermitian, and commute.
nodes.label: NoFreeFiniteDimQM_Theorem

nodes.name: Nonexistence of a differentiation operator as a finite-dimensional commutator
nodes.statement: There are no finite-dimensional operators $\hat{A}$ and $\hat{B}$ such that \begin{align} \commut{ f(\hat{A}), \hat{B} } = f'(\hat{A}) \end{align} for any ``good'' function $f(z)$.
nodes.section: 3 Revealing Inconsistencies in Finite-dimensional Quantum and Classical Mechanics
conclusions: There are no finite-dimensional operators $\hat{A}$ and $\hat{B}$ such that \begin{align} \commut{ f(\hat{A}), \hat{B} } = f'(\hat{A}) \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: No finite-dimensional operators can realize $\commut{f(\hat{A}),\hat{B}}=f'(\hat{A})$ for a general smooth $f$.
nodes.label: NoDiffAsCommutator_Theorem

nodes.name: Nonexistence of a finite-dimensional classical Liouvillian
nodes.statement: Let $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{p}$ be non-zero finite-dimensional Hermitian operators with $\commut{\hat{x}, \hat{p}} = 0$. There is no finite-dimensional operator $\hat{L}$ such that $i\commut{ \hat{L}, \hat{x} } = \hat{p}$.
nodes.section: 3 Revealing Inconsistencies in Finite-dimensional Quantum and Classical Mechanics
assumptions: Let $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{p}$ be non-zero finite-dimensional Hermitian operators with $\commut{\hat{x}, \hat{p}} = 0$.
conclusions: There is no finite-dimensional operator $\hat{L}$ such that $i\commut{ \hat{L}, \hat{x} } = \hat{p}$.
nodes.statement_short: No finite-dimensional $\hat{L}$ can generate the classical dynamics of commuting $\hat{x},\hat{p}$.
nodes.label: NoFiniteDimClassicalMecahnics

nodes.name: Non-Hermitian Hamiltonian vanishing lemma
nodes.statement: Assume that $\hat{x}$, $\hat{p}$, and $\hat{H}$ are bounded. If $\sigma(\hat{H}^{\dagger}) \cap \sigma(\hat{H}) = \emptyset$ and \begin{align} & im ( \hat{H}^{\dagger} \hat{x} - \hat{x} \hat{H} ) = \hbar \hat{p}, \\ & \hat{H}^{\dagger} \hat{p} = \hat{p} \hat{H}, \end{align} then $\hat{p} = \hat{x} = 0$. Here, $\sigma(\hat{A})$ denotes the spectrum of an operator $\hat{A}$.
nodes.section: 5 Non-Hermitian Hamiltonian as an Unsuccessful Attempt to Fix Inconsistencies
nodes.statement_short: If $\hat{H},\hat{x},\hat{p}$ are bounded with disjoint spectra of $\hat{H}^{\dagger},\hat{H}$ and the stated commutator relations, then $\hat{x}=\hat{p}=0$.
nodes.label: NonHermitian_Lemma1

nodes.name: Nonexistence of the free particle for non-Hermitian finite-dimensional Hamiltonians
nodes.statement: Assume i) $\hat{H}$, $\hat{x}$, and $\hat{p}$ are finite-dimensional operators satisfying Eqs. (\ref{First_OperEq_for_NonHer_FreeHamiltonian}) and (\ref{Second_OperEq_for_NonHer_FreeHamiltonian}); ii) $\lim_{t \to +\infty} \left| \langle \Psi(t) \ket{\Psi(t)} \right| < \infty$, where $\ket{\Psi(t)}$ is a solution of Eq. (\ref{Sch_Eq_General_Form}); iii) the eigenvectors $\{ \ket{E_n} \}_{n=1}^N$ ($\hat{H}\ket{E_n} = E_n \ket{E_n}$, $n \in I \coloneqq \{1,2,\ldots,N\}$) span the entire Hilbert space. Then, $\hat{p} = 0$.
nodes.section: 5 Non-Hermitian Hamiltonian as an Unsuccessful Attempt to Fix Inconsistencies
assumptions: Assume i) $\hat{H}$, $\hat{x}$, and $\hat{p}$ are finite-dimensional operators satisfying Eqs. (\ref{First_OperEq_for_NonHer_FreeHamiltonian}) and (\ref{Second_OperEq_for_NonHer_FreeHamiltonian})
ii) $\lim_{t \to +\infty} \left| \langle \Psi(t) \ket{\Psi(t)} \right| < \infty$, where $\ket{\Psi(t)}$ is a solution of Eq. (\ref{Sch_Eq_General_Form})
iii) the eigenvectors $\{ \ket{E_n} \}_{n=1}^N$ ($\hat{H}\ket{E_n} = E_n \ket{E_n}$, $n \in I \coloneqq \{1,2,\ldots,N\}$) span the entire Hilbert space
nodes.statement_short: Under finite-dimensionality, bounded-norm evolution, and eigenbasis completeness, the non-Hermitian analogue of the free-particle equations forces $\hat{p}=0$.
nodes.label: NonHermitian_Theorem1

nodes.name: Proof of the nonexistence of the free particle (finite-dim. QM)
nodes.statement: Let $\ket{E_n}$ denote a joint eigenvector of $\hat{H}$ and $\hat{p}$ such that $\hat{H} \ket{E_n} = E_n \ket{E_n}$ and $\hat{p} \ket{E_n} = p_n \ket{E_n}$. Assuming that $i \commut{ \hat{H}, \hat{x} } = \hat{p}$, one obtains \begin{align} i \bra{E_n} \commut{ \hat{H}, \hat{x} } \ket{E_m} = i (E_n - E_m) \bra{E_n} \hat{x} \ket{E_m} = p_m \langle E_n \ket{E_m}, \end{align} $\forall n,m$. The special case of this identity, when $n=m$, reads $p_m = 0$, $\forall m$. This contradicts the assumption that $\hat{p}$ is a non-zero matrix.
nodes.section: 3 Revealing Inconsistencies in Finite-dimensional Quantum and Classical Mechanics
nodes.statement_short: Diagonalize in a joint $\hat{H},\hat{p}$ eigenbasis; the $n=m$ case forces $p_m=0$, contradicting $\hat{p}\neq0$.

nodes.name: Proof of the nonexistence of a differentiation commutator
nodes.statement: Let a function of an operator be defined as (see, e.g., Ref. \cite{Nazaikinskii1992}) \begin{align} f(\hat{A}) \coloneqq \int g(k) e^{ik\hat{A}} dk, \quad f'(\hat{A}) \coloneqq \int ik g(k) e^{ik\hat{A}} dk, \notag \end{align} where $g(k)$ is the Fourier transform of a function $f(z)$. The correctness of Eq. (\ref{NoDiffAsCommutator_Eq1}) implies \begin{align} \commut{ e^{ik\hat{A}}, \hat{B} } = ik e^{ik\hat{A}}. \end{align} Differentiating the last identity with respect to $k$ and setting $k=0$, we reach the contradiction $\commut{ \hat{A}, \hat{B} } = 1$.
nodes.section: 3 Revealing Inconsistencies in Finite-dimensional Quantum and Classical Mechanics
nodes.statement_short: Differentiate the exponentiated-commutator identity at $k=0$ to force $[\hat{A},\hat{B}]=1$, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Proof of the nonexistence of a finite-dimensional classical Liouvillian
nodes.statement: Up to the notation ($\hat{H} \leftrightarrow \hat{x}$ and $\hat{x} \leftrightarrow \hat{L}$), this theorem is the same as Theorem \ref{NoFreeFiniteDimQM_Theorem}.
nodes.section: 3 Revealing Inconsistencies in Finite-dimensional Quantum and Classical Mechanics

nodes.name: Proof of the non-Hermitian vanishing lemma
nodes.statement: First, we employ the Rosenblum theorem \cite{Rosenblum1956} (see Theorem 9.3 in Ref. \cite{Bhatia1997}) to Eq. (\ref{First_OperEq_for_NonHer_FreeHamiltonian}) and then employ Eq. (\ref{Second_OperEq_for_NonHer_FreeHamiltonian}) to show \begin{align} im\hat{x} =& \frac{\hbar}{2\pi i} \oint_{\Gamma} d\xi ( \hat{H}^{\dagger} - \xi )^{-1} \hat{p} ( \hat{H} - \xi )^{-1} \notag\\ =& \frac{\hbar}{2\pi i} \hat{p} \oint_{\Gamma} d\xi ( \hat{H} - \xi )^{-2} = 0, \end{align} where $\Gamma$ denotes a union of closed contours in the complex plane with total winding numbers $1$ around $\sigma(\hat{H}^{\dagger})$ and $0$ around $\sigma(\hat{H})$.
nodes.section: 5 Non-Hermitian Hamiltonian as an Unsuccessful Attempt to Fix Inconsistencies
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Rosenblum theorem to a contour-integral representation to show $im\hat{x}=0$.

nodes.name: Proof of the nonexistence of the free particle (non-Hermitian case)
nodes.statement: Suppose $\hat{p} \neq 0$. According to Lyapunov stability theory \cite{Lyapunov1992}, the second assumption implies that $\Im(E_n) \leqslant 0$, $\forall n\in I$. Lemma \ref{NonHermitian_Lemma1} guarantees that $\hat{H}$ has at least a single real eigenvalue. Introduce $R \coloneqq \{ n \in I \, | \, \Im(E_n) = 0 \} \neq \emptyset$ -- the set of the real eigenvalues' indices. ``Sandwiching'' Eqs. (\ref{First_OperEq_for_NonHer_FreeHamiltonian}) and (\ref{Second_OperEq_for_NonHer_FreeHamiltonian}) leads to \begin{align} & im ( E_k^* - E_l ) \bra{E_k} \hat{x} \ket{E_l} = \hbar \bra{E_k} \hat{p} \ket{E_l}, \\ & ( E_k^* - E_l ) \bra{E_k} \hat{p} \ket{E_l} = 0, \qquad \forall k,l \in I. \end{align} According to Eq. (\ref{NonHermTh1_Eq2}), $\bra{E_k} \hat{p} \ket{E_l}$ may be non-zero only for $(k,l) \in Q \coloneqq \{ (k,l) \in R \times R \, | \, E_k = E_l \}$. However, Eq. (\ref{NonHermTh1_Eq1}) enforces $\bra{E_k} \hat{p} \ket{E_l} = 0$, $\forall (k,l) \in Q$. Therefore, we reach the contradiction $\hat{p} = 0$.
nodes.section: 5 Non-Hermitian Hamiltonian as an Unsuccessful Attempt to Fix Inconsistencies
nodes.statement_short: Assume $\hat{p}\neq0$; Lyapunov stability and Lemma 1 force a real eigenvalue, but sandwiching the hypothesis equations forces the corresponding matrix element of $\hat{p}$ to vanish — contradiction.

nodes.name: Coordinate and momentum operators (finite-dimensional)
nodes.statement: The left-hand side of Eq. (\ref{PhysOrigin_CCR}) is well defined in a finite-dimensional space, whereas the right-hand side of Eq. (\ref{PhysOrigin_CCR}) is not because no bounded operators obey the canonical commutation relation \cite{Weyl1950, Reed1980}. Thus, in the literature on finite-dimensional quantum mechanics, the coordinate and momentum operators are usually defined as those whose eigenvectors obey \begin{align} \langle x_n \ket{p_k} = \exp(i2\pi n k /N) / \sqrt{N}, \end{align} where $n,k = -j, -j+1, \ldots, j-1, j$, $j =2N+1$, $\hat{x} \ket{x_n} = an\ket{x_n}$, $\hat{p} \ket{p_k} = 2\pi \hbar k/(aN) \ket{p_k}$, and $N$ is the Hilbert space's dimension (see Ref. \cite{DelaTorre2003a} for a detailed description of the notation).
nodes.statement_short: Finite-dimensional $\hat{x},\hat{p}$ are usually defined via the mutually-unbiased-basis overlap relation, since no bounded operators satisfy the CCR.
nodes.section: 2 Mathematical Background

nodes.name: Mutually unbiased bases
nodes.statement: According to Eq. (\ref{Deff_PX_as_MUBS}), the coordinate and momentum eigenvectors form mutually unbiased bases, which means that if a system is prepared in a state from one of the bases, then all outcomes of the measurement with respect to the other basis are equally probable.
nodes.section: 2 Mathematical Background
differentia: if a system is prepared in a state from one of the bases, then all outcomes of the measurement with respect to the other basis are equally probable

nodes.name: Liouvillian
nodes.statement: As thoroughly elaborated in Ref. \cite{Bondar2011c}, the Liouvillian $\hat{L}$, the classical dynamics' generator, is a solution of the equations: $im\commut{ \hat{L}, \hat{x} } = \hat{p}$ and $i\commut{\hat{L}, \hat{p}} = -U'(\hat{x})$ with commuting $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{p}$.
nodes.statement_short: The Liouvillian $\hat{L}$ is defined as the generator solving the classical analogues of the commutator equations.
nodes.section: 3 Revealing Inconsistencies in Finite-dimensional Quantum and Classical Mechanics
differentia: is a solution of the equations: $im\commut{ \hat{L}, \hat{x} } = \hat{p}$ and $i\commut{\hat{L}, \hat{p}} = -U'(\hat{x})$ with commuting $\hat{x}$ and $\hat{p}$

nodes.name: Stone's theorem (uniqueness of the generator)
nodes.statement: Stone's theorem (see, e.g., Ref. \cite{Reed1980, Araujo2008}) guarantees the uniqueness of the Hermitian operator $\hat{H}$ in Eq. (\ref{Sch_Eq_General_Form}).
nodes.section: 3 Revealing Inconsistencies in Finite-dimensional Quantum and Classical Mechanics

nodes.name: General Hamiltonian satisfying the first Ehrenfest theorem
nodes.statement: Assuming $\hat{x}$ is Hermitian and has a non-degenerate spectrum, the solution of Eq. (\ref{First_CommutEq_for_Hamiltonian}) is \begin{align} \bra{x_k} \hat{H}^{\star} \ket{x_l} = \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} U(x_k) + C & \mbox{if } k=l \\ \frac{i \hbar \bra{x_k} \hat{p} \ket{x_l} }{m(x_k - x_l)} &\mbox{otherwise} \end{array} \right. \end{align} where $\hat{x} \ket{x_l} = x_l \ket{x_l}$ and $C$ is an arbitrary real constant. For any definition of the momentum operator $\hat{p}$, Eq. (\ref{Ehrenfest_Compartible_GeneralHamiltonian}) provides the most general Hamiltonian obeying the first Ehrenfest theorem [Eq. (\ref{EhrenfestTh1})].
nodes.statement_short: Any Hamiltonian obeying the first Ehrenfest theorem has diagonal entries $U(x_k)+C$ and off-diagonal entries fixed by $\hat{p}$.

assumptions: Assuming $\hat{x}$ is Hermitian and has a non-degenerate spectrum

(\ref{First_CommutEq_for_Hamiltonian}) is \begin{align} \bra{x_k} \hat{H}^{\star} \ket{x_l} = \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} U(x_k) + C & \mbox{if } k=l \\ \frac{i \hbar \bra{x_k} \hat{p} \ket{x_l} }{m(x_k - x_l)} &\mbox{otherwise} \end{array} \right. \end{align} where $\hat{x} \ket{x_l} = x_l \ket{x_l}$ and $C$ is an arbitrary real constant.

For any definition of the momentum operator $\hat{p}$, Eq. (\ref{Ehrenfest_Compartible_GeneralHamiltonian}) provides the most general Hamiltonian obeying the first Ehrenfest theorem [Eq. (\ref{EhrenfestTh1})].

nodes.name: MUB-based vs. standard Hamiltonian under the Ehrenfest theorem
nodes.statement: Let $\hat{H}_{mub}^{\star}$ denote the Hamiltonian (\ref{Ehrenfest_Compartible_GeneralHamiltonian}) after substituting $\hat{p}$ from Eq. (\ref{Deff_PX_as_MUBS}), and $\hat{H}_{mub}$ be the Hamiltonian (\ref{Infinite_Dim_Form_Hamiltonian}) with the same $\hat{p}$. Contrary to $\hat{H}_{mub}^{\star}$, the matrix $\hat{H}_{mub}$ does not satisfy the Ehrenfest theorem (\ref{EhrenfestTh1}).
nodes.statement_short: Compares the MUB-based and standard finite-dimensional Hamiltonians' compliance with the first Ehrenfest theorem.
nodes.section: 4 Inconsistencies and Numerical Calculations

nodes.name: No correlation between numerical accuracy and Ehrenfest-theorem compliance
nodes.statement: This exercise demonstrates [Fig. \ref{Fig_EigenvectorComparison}(a)] that even though the Hamiltonian $\hat{H}_{fd}^{\star}$ reproduces the exact energy better than either $\hat{H}_{mub}^{\star}$ or $\hat{H}_{mub}$, it yields poor quality excited states. Finally, note that the Hamiltonian $\hat{H}_{mub}^{\star}$, satisfying Ehrenfest theorem (\ref{EhrenfestTh1}), provides results of the same quality as $\hat{H}_{mub}$, violating Eq. (\ref{EhrenfestTh1}). These observations indicate that there is no correlation between the numerical calculations' accuracy and the Ehrenfest theorem's validity.
nodes.section: 4 Inconsistencies and Numerical Calculations

nodes.name: Physical interpretation: nonexistence of the free particle
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{NoFreeFiniteDimQM_Theorem} physically implies the nonexistence of the ``free'' particle in finite-dimensional quantum mechanics. This statement is also a consequence of probability conservation, closely linked to Stone's theorem. If the wave function's normalization is constant and $\hat{x}$ is finite-dimensional, then the particle's motion is confined to the spatial interval bound by the smallest and largest eigenvalues of $\hat{x}$. This confinement must be realized by some force. Since standalone Eq. (\ref{First_CommutEq_for_Hamiltonian}) is solvable with respect to $\hat{H}$ [see Eq. (\ref{Ehrenfest_Compartible_GeneralHamiltonian}) below], then $i \commut{ \hat{H}, \hat{p} }/\hbar$ from Eq. (\ref{Second_CommutEq_for_Hamiltonian}) can be taken as the definition of this confining force.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 1's no-free-particle result motivates defining a confining force from the unsatisfied commutator equation.
nodes.section: 3 Revealing Inconsistencies in Finite-dimensional Quantum and Classical Mechanics

nodes.name: Ehrenfest theorems fail for a particle in a box
nodes.statement: Note that the Ehrenfest theorems do not hold for a particle in a box even in the infinite-dimensional case \cite{Alonso2000}.
nodes.section: 3 Revealing Inconsistencies in Finite-dimensional Quantum and Classical Mechanics

nodes.name: Ambiguity in defining potential force
nodes.statement: Theorem \ref{NoDiffAsCommutator_Theorem} establishes not only the nonsolvability of Eq. (\ref{Second_CommutEq_for_Hamiltonian}) but also two nonequivalent definitions ($\hat{F} = - U'(\hat{x})$ and $\hat{F} = i\commut{U(\hat{x}), \hat{p}}/\hbar$) of a potential force $\hat{F}$ in a finite-dimensional framework. The latter definition should be preferred due to the comment after Theorem \ref{NoFreeFiniteDimQM_Theorem}.
nodes.statement_short: Theorem 2 implies two inequivalent finite-dimensional definitions of potential force; the commutator-based one is preferred.
nodes.section: 3 Revealing Inconsistencies in Finite-dimensional Quantum and Classical Mechanics

nodes.name: A nonstandard-analysis route around the no-go theorems
nodes.statement: In particular, a key element in proving theorems \ref{NoFreeFiniteDimQM_Theorem} and \ref{NoFiniteDimClassicalMecahnics} is the non-existence of a finite real number $r$ such that $0\cdot r \neq 0$. However, this equation has a solution if infinitesimal and infinitely-large numbers are included into the set of real numbers. Thus, some of the no-go theorems may be avoided by utilizing nonstandard analysis \cite{robert2003nonstandard, Almeida2004}, where such extensions are rigorously implemented.
